subject: AI & Agents
title: AI Bias: Reflecting Our Worst
description: One-minute skill: AI Bias: Reflecting Our Worst.

hook.text: An AI hiring tool at Amazon penalized resumes containing the word 'women's.' Amazon scrapped it.

buildup.text: AI learns from historical data. If that data contains bias, the AI reproduces and amplifies it.

discovery.text: Bias isn't a bug — it's a mirror. AI reflects the patterns in the data humans created.

twist.text: Fixing bias in AI is hard because it requires agreeing on what fairness means — and humans disagree.

climax.text: Despite awareness, biased AI systems are still deployed in criminal justice, lending, and healthcare.

punchline.text: Garbage in, bias out. The machine learns what we teach it.

quiz.question: Why did Amazon's AI hiring tool discriminate against women?
options: It learned from historical hiring data that reflected existing gender bias
It was intentionally programmed to discriminate
Women submitted fewer resumes to Amazon

details.summary: AI systems learn biases from their training data, reflecting and sometimes amplifying society's prejudices. The myth that AI is inherently objective obscures how bias enters through human-created datasets.
details.whyItMatters: Believing AI is objective lets biased systems operate unchallenged. Recognizing AI as a mirror of human data helps drive demands for fairness audits and diverse training data.
takeaways: AI inherits biases embedded in its training data
The objectivity myth lets biased systems escape scrutiny
Bias awareness drives better data practices and auditing

faq.question: How does bias get into AI systems?
faq.answer: Through training data that reflects historical human biases. If hiring data shows past discrimination, the AI learns to replicate those patterns. Bias enters through data, not through the algorithm itself.

faq.question: Can AI bias be completely eliminated?
faq.answer: Not entirely, since some bias is inherent in any real-world data. However, it can be significantly reduced through diverse datasets, bias testing, and ongoing monitoring after deployment.
